第 26 章 Fire Them!开掉他们！

Mike Fisher / 迈克·费舍尔

— 第 79 页 —

Fire them! As people managers, we all must deal with personnel who are not performing to our standards or are displaying behaviors that are not aligned with our culture. This sounds very cut and dried, but in most cases it's not. The work that engineers perform is usually multifaceted, and the required competencies are broad. Typically, we need engineers to write code, fix bugs, achieve business results, participate in Agile ceremonies, mentor other engineers, and more. To do these effectively, we need engineers to be great written and verbal communicators, be leaders, be knowledgeable, be collaborative, and be effective, to name just a few competencies.

开掉他们！作为人员经理，我们都必须处理那些不达标准或行为与文化不符的人。这听起来很干脆，但大多数时候不是。工程师的工作通常是多方面的，所需能力也很广。通常我们需要工程师写代码、修 bug、达成业务结果、参加敏捷仪式、辅导其他工程师等等。要有效地做这些，我们需要工程师是优秀的书面和口头沟通者、是领导者、知识渊博、善于协作、高效——这还只是列举几项能力。

Often, we are faced with scenarios in which a person is displaying all the correct behaviors but they are not delivering. Or, they are achieving their goals but they are doing it in a manner not in line with your culture. Often times some of our most brilliant engineers are curmudgeons who can't work well with others. I call these engineers "brilliant jerks." It's unfortunate for them because much of engineering is team based.

我们经常面临这样的场景：一个人表现出所有正确的行为但没有产出。或者，他们在达成目标，但方式不符合你的文化。很多时候我们最聪明的工程师是些脾气古怪、无法和他人好好合作的人。我叫这些工程师「聪明的混蛋」。对他们来说不幸的是，工程大部分是基于团队的。

What sounds so clear on paper is often a confusing scenario in which engineering managers become stuck trying to decide whether they have given the engineer enough time to improve or whether a different coaching technique will fix everything. In these scenarios, my guidance to managers is to take action quickly. It's better for the company to begin looking for the replacement and the open position will add some urgency. It's also better for the individual. If they are performing poorly or not behaving well, they should already be aware of it because of all the clear communication you have had with them. These conversations are stressful for everyone, the person giving it and the person receiving it. Keeping the person in this limbo state for a long period of time is super stressful. It is better to let them go so they can find a role more suitable to their skills or a team whose culture is more suited to their behaviors.

纸面上听起来很清楚的事情，往往是令人困惑的场景——工程经理纠结于是否给了工程师足够的改进时间，或者换一种辅导技巧能不能解决一切。在这些场景中，我给经理的建议是快速行动。公司开始找替补更好，空缺职位会增加紧迫感。对个人也更好。如果他们表现不好或行为不当，因为你已经和他们进行了所有清晰的沟通，他们应该已经意识到了。这些对话对每个人都有压力——给出的人和接收的人。让一个人长期处于这种悬而未决的状态压力极大。让他们走更好，这样他们可以找到更适合自己技能的角色或文化更适合自己行为的团队。

— 第 80 页 —

But wait, you say! I can't let them go because everyone else will leave, or everything will break, or everyone will hate me. I've seen scores of personnel issues for which managers used these types of excuses to avoid taking action and yet, I have never seen any of these terrible scenarios actually happen. Let's take these one by one and examine the reality:

但是，你说！我不能让他们走，因为其他人会走，或者一切都会崩溃，或者所有人都会恨我。我见过几十起人员问题，经理们用这些借口来避免采取行动，但我从未见过任何这些可怕场景真正发生。让我们一个一个来审视现实：

Everyone will leave. It is true that in many markets engineering unemployment is nearly zero and engineers can find another position almost immediately. However, their departure is still not very likely. Hopefully, most of your engineers love your culture and your mission. They are there in support of something larger than themselves or another individual. The departure of even one key individual usually doesn't undermine the noble mission of the company. Also, unless your team is composed of nothing but junior engineers, they have experienced the frequent departure of friends, colleagues, and managers.

所有人都会走。确实，在很多市场工程岗位失业率几乎为零，工程师几乎可以立刻找到另一个职位。然而，他们的离开仍然不太可能。希望你的大多数工程师热爱你的文化和使命。他们在那里支持比自己或另一个人更伟大的事业。即使一个关键人物离开，通常也不会动摇公司的崇高使命。而且，除非你的团队全是初级工程师，他们已经历过朋友、同事和经理的频繁离职。

Everything will break. As a manager, one of your many responsibilities is to not allow SPOFs (single points of failure) to exist in the system or on the team. Long before you need to ask someone to leave or someone decides that they want to leave, you should be thinking about succession plans. Even if you've failed to adequately plan for this eventual scenario, there are other really smart people, possibly already in your organization, who if given a chance can step up.

一切都会崩溃。作为经理，你的众多责任之一是不允许系统或团队中存在单点故障（SPOF）。早在你需要请人离开或某人决定要走之前，你就应该思考继任计划。即使你没有充分规划这个最终场景，还有其他非常聪明的人——可能已经在你的组织里——如果给机会就能站出来。

Everyone will hate me. If your team has an underperforming or misbehaving individual, the entire team already knows. Every other engineer on the team is quite aware of who pulls their own weight, who puts forth the extra effort, and who is a pleasure to work with. Dismissal of individuals with behavior that is misaligned to the culture is almost universally lauded by the remaining teammates.

所有人都会恨我。如果你的团队有一个表现不佳或行为不当的人，整个团队早就知道了。团队里每个其他工程师都很清楚谁在尽力、谁在额外付出、谁合作愉快。解雇与文化行为不符的人几乎总是被留下来的队友称赞。

The short of it is that moving fast to get someone out of your organization is almost always the correct thing to do for the company as well as for the individual. Leaving underperformers or badly behaving individuals on a team is affecting the entire team, adding unnecessary stress, and likely not mitigating any real risks.

简而言之，快速把人请出组织几乎总是对公司和个人都正确的事。把表现不佳或行为不端的人留在团队里影响整个团队，增加不必要的压力，而且可能并没有减轻任何真正的风险。
